concepts.def: Sense of self constructed through interaction with others; both personal (individual) and social (group) dimensions.
Process of learning culture; primary in family, secondary through school, media, peers, religion and work.
Goffman (1959): social life is theatre; we present a 'front-stage' self while managing 'back-stage' identities.
Increased worldwide interconnection through trade, media and migration; produces hybrid identities (Hall 1992).
Bauman (2000) 'liquid modernity': identity is fluid, fragmented and self-chosen through consumption.
Baudrillard (1981): media simulations become more real than reality; identity formed by consumed signs.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Culture, Identity & Socialisation — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Culture, Identity & Socialisation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Culture, Identity & Socialisation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Goffman
Hall

Bauman

Hall
Goffman
The most important socialisation, happening in school.
Learning facts in primary school.
Radical feminists oppose all women's rights.
Early learning of norms and values, primarily within the family.

mcqs.q: What is the Marxist view on white-collar crime?
options: It is treated more harshly than street crime.
It does not really happen - only the working class commit crime.
It is widespread but under-policed because law serves ruling-class interests.
Radical feminists oppose all women's rights.

mcqs.q: How does radical feminism differ from liberal feminism?
options: Radical feminists oppose all women's rights.
Radical feminists see patriarchy as the primary system of oppression requiring fundamental change.
They are essentially the same with minor differences.
It is treated more harshly than street crime.
